title: The Temp
logline: Michael gives the new temp, Ryan, a day-long orientation he did not ask for, Dwight decides Ryan is a corporate spy, and Jim and Pam compete to make Dwight say 'beets'.
outline: A: Michael gives Ryan an exhaustive orientation and tries to impress him, including with Jan on speakerphone. B: Jim and Pam's game: who can get Dwight to say 'beets' more times by five. C: Dwight interrogates Ryan as a corporate spy. Order: cold, A, B, A, C, B, A, A, B, C, A, B, tag
theme: First impressions, and who we try to impress
storySoFar: Ryan Howard started as the temp at Dunder Mifflin Scranton; he's in business school and plans to leave in two months. Michael gave him an exhaustive orientation and his old red stapler, and keeps mentioning Jan Levinson from corporate, who asked to be taken off speakerphone. Dwight thinks Ryan is a corporate spy because branches are rumored to be closing, and keeps a dossier on him (Angela agrees he looks untrustworthy). Kelly calls Ryan 'Ry-Ry'. Jim and Pam's game: Pam got Dwight to say 'beets' eleven times and won a Twix. Pam is engaged to Roy, who honks from the parking lot.

stateChanges.progress: Ryan started; Michael idolizes him, Kelly calls him Ry-Ry, Dwight thinks he's a spy
The beets game; Pam won a Twix; Roy honked; Jim's talking head gave him away a little
Michael talks about Jan constantly; Dwight has heard branches may close

stateChanges.status: Kelly has decided he's cute and calls him Ry-Ry

stateChanges.text: Michael gave Ryan his first stapler, a battered red one from 1993
Jim and Pam's daily games against Dwight (beets count, front-desk pages)

scenes.recap: Pam pages Dwight to the front desk over and over; every time he arrives, she's on a call.

beats.text: Dwight Schrute to the front desk, please. Dwight Schrute.
Yes? What is it? Is it a package? Is it a threat?

beats.caption: holds up one finger, deep in a phone call

beats.text: Dwight Schrute to the front desk.

lines: That's nine. Pam's record is fourteen.
It was a slow Tuesday. We don't talk about that Tuesday.

scenes.recap: Michael introduces the new temp, Ryan, with a speech, and keeps mentioning a 'very important lady from corporate'.

beats.text: Everybody, big day. We have a new member of the Dunder Mifflin family. Like an adoption. But legal.
Hi. I'm Ryan. I'm the temp.
Ryan is in business school. Which is like real school, but for money.
And a very important lady from corporate approved his hire personally. Jan. Levinson. Gould. Just Levinson now.
Is this meeting about the temp or the lady?
It's about family, Stanley.

lines: I don't have kids. Yet. I have the office.
And today the office had a baby, and the baby is Ryan.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam set today's game: whoever gets Dwight to say 'beets' the most by five wins.

beats.text: New game. Whoever gets Dwight to say 'beets' the most times by five o'clock wins.
What do I win?
The respect of a nation. And a Twix from the machine.
Deal. Loser buys the Twix.

beats.caption: draws a scoreboard on a sticky note: JIM / PAM

lines: Jim and I have a lot of games. It makes the day go faster.
Roy says it's weird. Roy doesn't work up here, though.

scenes.recap: Michael takes Ryan to the warehouse to show off his 'street' rapport with Darryl, who is not having it.

beats.text: Darryl! My brother from a different... warehouse. Ryan, this is where the magic happens.
The magic is boxes, man.
Darryl, tell Ryan how we say hello down here.
We say 'hello.'
Hello, dog.
Hey.

lines: I'm here to learn how a small business runs. For school.
So far I've learned the warehouse is cold and Michael says 'dog.'

scenes.recap: Dwight corners Ryan at the vending machine and interrogates him as a suspected corporate spy.

beats.text: Name. Rank. True purpose.
Ryan. Temp. Getting a granola bar.
Business school. The West Point of spies. Who sent you?
A temp agency. In Wilkes-Barre.
That's exactly what a spy from Wilkes-Barre would say.

lines: Corporate is closing branches. Everybody knows. Nobody has said it. I know.
And then a 'temp' appears. Temp is short for temptation. Or temperature. Either way: suspicious.

scenes.recap: Jim gets Dwight to say 'beets' three times with a fake question about root vegetables.

beats.text: Dwight, settle something. Strongest root vegetable. Carrots, right?
Carrots? False. Beets. Beets have a higher density, beets store for months, and beets can stain a man for life.
Interesting.

scenes.recap: Michael introduces Ryan to the annex; Kelly gives Ryan a nickname, and Michael is cruel to Toby for no reason.

beats.text: And this is the annex. Kelly, customer service. Toby, nothing.
HR, actually. Hi, Ryan. If you ever need—
He won't need. Nobody needs.
Oh my God, you're so cute. I'm going to call you Ry-Ry. Is that okay? It's happening.
I'd prefer Ryan.
Okay, Ry-Ry.

scenes.recap: To impress Ryan, Michael puts Jan on speakerphone; she asks to be taken off speaker immediately.

beats.caption: dials corporate and hits speaker with a flourish

beats.text: Jan! It's Michael. I'm here with Ryan, the temp you approved. Say hi to Ryan.
She says take her off speaker. She's playing hard to get. Very corporate.
I think she means take her off speaker.

lines: Jan and I have a very professional relationship. She's my boss. I'm her... employee.
There's tension. Not bad tension. Sexy tension. Professionally.

scenes.recap: Pam asks Dwight one innocent question about the farm and scores eleven 'beets'.

beats.text: Dwight, how's the farm this time of year?
The beets are in the cellar, the beet greens are composted, the beet seed is drying, and the beet—
FOUR MINUTES LATER
—which is why beets are the true king of the cellar. Thank you for asking. Nobody asks.

beats.caption: writes '11' on the scoreboard under PAM

scenes.recap: Dwight reveals his dossier on Ryan to Angela; Ryan overhears and doesn't care.

beats.caption: slides a thin manila folder labeled RYAN (SPY?) to Angela

beats.text: He drinks his coffee black. Like a man with nothing to hide. Which is what a man with something to hide would do.
He seems untrustworthy. He has bangs.
I can hear you. I'm right here.
Good. Now you know you're being watched.

scenes.recap: At the end of the day, Michael tells Ryan about his own first day, and gives him his old stapler.

beats.text: My first day here was 1993. I wore a tie with a fish on it. Nobody talked to me until Thursday.
So. I just wanted your first day to be better than mine.

beats.caption: hands Ryan a battered red stapler

beats.text: This was my first stapler. It's been through a lot. It's seen things.
Thanks, Michael. That's... actually nice.

lines: My plan was to stay two months and learn what not to do.
I've learned a lot of what not to do. Also, I have a stapler.

scenes.recap: At five, Pam collects her Twix; Roy honks from the truck, and Jim watches her go.

beats.caption: hands over a Twix, with ceremony

beats.text: Eleven. I'll never recover. My children will hear of this.
Tell them their dad lost to a girl with a farm question.
Pam! Let's go! Traffic!
Coming! Bye, Jim. Good game.

lines: Best part of the day? Probably that. Losing a Twix.

scenes.recap: Creed introduces himself to Ryan, and Ryan wishes he hadn't.

beats.text: You're the new guy. I'm Creed. If anybody asks, you've never seen me.
We work in the same office.
And yet.
